title: Wine Wimsey Review · Mon Nov 23
subtitle: NEW-VOICE test batch 1 (replaces the earlier old-style 7+2 Nov 23 batch.json; those PNGs remain in this folder). 8 character feed posts + 2 stories. All posts use the locked cartoon character with a rotating expression and an action. Captions and first comments included. No TOBIs, no plain cards. Seasonal: none. Quotes: 10 original. Credits: GenerateImage (free). Scott accepted all 8 feed posts and said upload; the 2 stories were shown and taken as approved with that upload. First-comment delays randomized (mix of 0 and 1-20 minutes). Posting time blank so posts fill Scott's staggered Post Planner queue slots.

posts.quote: Call me crazy, but if I'm scanning, bagging, and weighing my own groceries, I want the employee discount. / Instead the screen asked me to round up for charity. / I AM the charity.
posts.caption: $187 on Saturday, two "unexpected item in bagging area" alerts, and one teenager watching six machines. I got home, poured a glass, and worked out my hourly wage. Zero.
posts.first: The round-up button sits right next to the pay button. That's not an accident.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses at a grocery self-checkout. She holds a bag and points at a screen that says Round up for charity?, with a large green Yes button, a small No thanks, and a wine bottle in the cart. Text at the top reads: Call me crazy, but if I'm scanning, bagging, and weighing my own groceries, I want the employee discount. Instead the screen asked me to round up for charity. A pink box at the bottom reads: I am the charity.
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: smug excuse-me squint, pointing at the screen

posts.quote: My parents raised three kids, paid off a house, and spent a week at the lake every summer on one income. / I have two jobs, a budget app, and a payment plan for my teeth. / Somebody explain what happened.
posts.caption: I'm not complaining about hard work. My dad worked hard. He just got something for it.
posts.first: My mother still asks why I don't just put a little away each month. With what, Mom.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. Then: a smiling family of five on a dock by a lake house. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses toasts with red wine at a kitchen table beside a laptop. Text at the top reads: My parents raised three kids, paid off a house, and spent a week at the lake every summer on one income. Text below reads: I have two jobs, a budget app, and a payment plan for my teeth. A purple box at the bottom reads: Somebody explain what happened.
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: tight fake 'everything is fine' smile, toasting with wine

posts.quote: I ordered at a counter. I filled my own drink. I carried my own tray. / And the iPad still wanted 25%. / For what, turning around?
posts.caption: $31 for two sandwiches on Tuesday, and the screen started at 22%. The girl watched me press "custom" like I was robbing the place.
posts.first: I tip well when somebody brings me food. I'm not tipping a touchscreen.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on an orange background. She smirks and points at a tablet with tip buttons for 25%, 30% and 35%. Text at the top reads: I ordered at a counter. I filled my own drink. I carried my own tray. And the iPad still wanted 25%. A teal box at the bottom reads: For what, turning around?
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: squinty smirk, pointing at the tip screen

posts.quote: I keep hearing nobody wants to work anymore. / Okay. Maybe. / But my niece just did three interviews and a personality test for a $14-an-hour job that wanted her seven days a week.
posts.caption: The fourth round was "a quick chat with the team." She never heard back, and the listing is still up.
posts.first: The rejection came at 11:48 on a Sunday night. Automated, of course.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses at a kitchen table, pointing at a laptop that says Assessment 4 of 6, while a younger woman in a hoodie looks tired. A glass of red wine sits on the table. Text at the top reads: I keep hearing nobody wants to work anymore. Okay. Maybe. An orange box at the bottom reads: But my niece just did three interviews and a personality test for a $14-an-hour job that wanted her seven days a week.
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: open-mouth jaw-drop, pointing at the laptop

posts.quote: In 1985 you called the doctor, a woman named Barb answered, and you were seen Thursday. / Now I need a portal, a password, and a chatbot named Ava who can fit me in March.
posts.caption: I just wanted someone to look at my shoulder. Instead I got a survey about my experience. Oh, I'll tell you about my experience, Ava.
posts.first: Barb knew your whole family by name. Ava doesn't know what a shoulder is.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1985: a receptionist hands a card to a younger woman beside a rotary phone. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses grimaces at a phone chat, holding her shoulder, wine on the table. Text at the top reads: In 1985 you called the doctor, a woman named Barb answered, and you were seen Thursday. A red box at the bottom reads: Now I need a portal, a password, and a chatbot named Ava who can fit me in March.
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: pained twitchy grimace at the chatbot, holding her shoulder

posts.quote: My homeowners insurance went up again because of 'market conditions.' / Twenty-two years. Zero claims. / I'm not the market. I'm just the one paying for it.
posts.caption: The letter was two pages long and said nothing. The woman on the phone told me everyone's going up. That isn't an explanation, it's a weather report.
posts.first: I asked what I could do to lower it. She suggested a higher deductible.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses on a yellow background, one hand on her hip, holding out a renewal notice with a red upward arrow. Text at the top reads: My homeowners insurance went up again because of "market conditions." Twenty-two years. Zero claims. A red box at the bottom reads: I'm not the market. I'm just the one paying for it.
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: unimpressed look, hand on hip, dangling the renewal letter

posts.quote: If you put your phone on speaker in a waiting room, / everyone within fifty yards gets a vote on the conversation. / And I vote you hang up.
posts.caption: Twenty minutes at the eye doctor hearing about Gary's boat, his ex-wife, and the boat his ex-wife got. Nobody asked. We all know about the boat now.
posts.first: His appointment was before mine. The quiet after he left was beautiful.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a waiting room. A woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses pulls her glasses down, side-eyes a man shouting into a phone held out on speaker, and raises one finger. Other people look annoyed. Text at the top reads: If you put your phone on speaker in a waiting room, everyone within fifty yards gets a vote on the conversation. A teal box at the bottom reads: And I vote you hang up.
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: side-eye over glasses pulled down, one finger raised to vote

posts.quote: The cable company called to thank me for 14 years of loyalty. / Then offered the new-customer price to everybody but me. / Apparently loyalty is a penalty now.
posts.caption: Forty minutes on hold to hear that the deal is only for new customers. I said fine, cancel me. Suddenly there was a deal.
posts.first: It's the same box, the same channels, and $61 less. Funny how that works.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on a purple background. She holds a phone to her ear, rolls her eyes, and holds up a bill with $189.99 circled in red. Text at the top reads: The cable company called to thank me for 14 years of loyalty. Then offered the new-customer price to everybody but me. An orange box at the bottom reads: Apparently loyalty is a penalty now.
posts.note: new-voice batch 1, personality redo approved Nov 22
posts.expression: slow eye-roll, bill held up as evidence, phone on hold

Now I need a phone, a QR code, and a full battery to order a hamburger. A pink box at the bottom reads: Just hand me the paper.
stories.expression: glasses pulled down, unimpressed look at a 4% battery
